pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – LIBRARY SKILLS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we get information on something we want to understand more?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. trace specific reading materials from online or print sources

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. trace specific reading materials from online or print sources
   In simple words: practise until you can trace specific reading materials from online or print sources. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills.
4. Show that you can: trace specific reading materials from online or print sources

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 2.2.1 Extensive reading – Library skills important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Search for texts related to technology, social media or the internet, using digital devices or the library,
2. List down the vocabulary identified from the read texts,
3. Pick out names of digital devices from the texts, read and write them on charts for display,
4. Prepare a reading log on the resources read including key details (e.g. title, author, main idea, vocabulary),
5. Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner effectively orders and prioritises tasks when conducting a silent reading session.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we get information on something we want to understand more?
2. Why is it important to use the internet safely and cautiously?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. trace specific reading materials from online or print sources

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
